avertissement: Traductions automatiques des textes français ; chaque nombre a été vérifié contre le français. Les documents de la Ville sont en français et font foi.

canopee.description: Tree planting, greening, fighting emerald ash borer and heat islands.
canopee.enBref: The City buys trees and has them planted on public land, and it pays an organization to green private and institutional lots. Boroughs are adding their own resources: money from the parks fund, equipment rental, blue-collar crews. Exemptions also govern tree planting in two building projects.

etapes.texte: City council awards contracts to 7574479 Canada inc. and Terrassement Technique Sylvain Labrecque inc. to supply and plant 1,374 trees, then water them, maintain them and replace some of them. The maximum expense is $2,456,590.55, taxes included, for trees spread across seven boroughs.

Pierrefonds-Roxboro transfers up to $162,233.12 from its reserved parks fund to buy trees and plants. City council pays $3,071,550 to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain to plant and maintain trees on private and institutional sites from March 24 to December 31, 2026.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve authorizes an addition at 1620, rue Préfontaine with 25 trees and 5% greening instead of the required 40 trees and 25%. Montréal-Nord allows trees to be planted less than 1.5 metres from the street line at 5745, boulevard Léger, for a two-storey building.

Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve rents a mini backhoe loader with operator for $152,916.75, taxes included, and sets aside $200,000 for additional blue-collar crews assigned to planting, from May to November 2026. Outremont entrusts URBEX Construction inc. with the renovation of the parc Pratt chalet and the redevelopment of its surroundings, including plant planting, partly funded by the Programme de réfection et de verdissement des parcs locaux.

City council leases land in the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain for a total rent of $100 before taxes. The organization stores materials, equipment and trees for planting there.

aSurveiller.texte: The Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain must submit its accountability report by December 31, 2026 at the latest, then its report and financial statements by March 31, 2027.
The lease for the Namur-Hippodrome neighbourhood nursery runs until April 30, 2028.

eau-egouts.description: Pipes, drinking water production plants, Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, retention basins.
eau-egouts.enBref: This year, the City is funding and launching work on its water and sewer pipes, both in borough streets and on the main network. It is also awarding several contracts at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, including the construction of the oxygen production unit linked to the disinfection project. The replacement of lead service connections, including the portion located on private land, comes up in a large number of decisions.

etapes.texte: The City is raising from $197,000,000 to $381,000,000 the loan that funds the disinfection unit for the effluent at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant. The money is used to finish the ozonation unit, install liquid oxygen tanks and build the oxygen production plant.

The City is awarding a series of contracts to rehabilitate secondary water pipes without digging a trench and to redo the roadway, in streets across several boroughs. Each contract includes the replacement of lead water service connections on both the public side and the private side.

The urban agglomeration council is adopting a $12,000,000 loan for main pipes in the Namur–De la Savane area and amending the fee schedule of the by-law delegating maintenance of the main network to related municipalities. A notice of motion is given for a $951,000,000 loan intended for the renewal of secondary waterworks and sewer networks.

aSurveiller.texte: Announced adoption of the $951,000,000 loan by-law for the renewal of secondary waterworks and sewer networks, on October 19, 2026.
The rehabilitation work on the 600 mm pipe along autoroute 15 Nord must be completed by December 18, 2026 at the latest.
Shutdown of sludge incinerator 2 in the first week of October 2026 and of incinerator 4 in January 2027, for about six weeks of work each.
End of the water pipe rehabilitation work on rue de la Cathédrale postponed from December 2026 to March 2027.
Work site on rue Guy between Saint-Jacques and René-Lévesque until December 2027; commissioning of the ozone plant planned for 2029.

frederic-back.titre: Parc Frédéric-Back and Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel
frederic-back.description: The former quarry turned dump, being transformed into a park in phases: urban greenhouses, biogas capture, and electrical system upgrades.
frederic-back.enBref: This year, the City is moving forward on three fronts at parc Frédéric-Back and the Complexe environnemental Saint-Michel: a greenhouse complex in the Saint-Michel neighbourhood, the modernization of electrical facilities linked to biogas capture, and park maintenance. It is also requesting financial assistance from Quebec for an east-west pedestrian and bike link with a footbridge. At the same time, the borough is redoing rue De Louvain, along the edge of the park.

etapes.titre: Funding request for the east-west link
etapes.texte: The City is asking the Quebec Ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable for assistance of up to $2,000,000 for a 900-metre trail crossing the park from east to west, including a footbridge of about 150 metres (CG26 0121). The project also includes rainwater management works and a 12.7-hectare meadow.

The agglomeration approves the construction of a research, training and community production greenhouse complex, valued at $2,185,000, then delegates the project to city council (CG26 0124). The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension offers to carry it out and city council accepts (CA26 14 0039, CM26 0363).

The City awards Systèmes Urbains inc. a contract worth $1,091,693.37, taxes included, for the second phase of electrical work at the Complexe environnemental de Saint-Michel, which includes a new 25 kV power supply, a backup generator and a controller to manage biogas capture (CG26 0223). It also entrusts two companies with the general maintenance and ecological and horticultural management of the park for 30 months (CG26 0224).

The borough entrusts Groupe MPotvin with the redevelopment of rue De Louvain, between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum amount of $8,199,514.82, taxes included, and authorizes total spending of $11,192,464.62. The work covers sewers and water mains, lighting, traffic lights, sidewalks, the bike path and plantings.

The City is extending by five months the rental of a compost screener and a loader tractor with operator at the Complexe environnemental de Saint-Michel, for an additional $296,349.21, taxes included. The compost, made from leaves collected in parks and streets, is used in particular for the development of parc Frédéric-Back (CG26 0320).

The borough entrusts Les industries Harnois inc. with the supply and installation of the greenhouse complex, for a maximum amount of $499,865.92, taxes included, and authorizes total spending of $574,845.80. The project involves two greenhouses with structure, envelope, natural ventilation, flooring, interior partitions and condensation water management.

aSurveiller.texte: Greenhouses: delivery of infrastructure in July 2026, work starting in August 2026 and expected completion in December 2026, according to the borough's file.
Greenhouses expected to be in service by winter 2027.
The call for projects under the Ministère des Transports' assistance program, for the footbridge and east-west link, ends on November 26, 2026.
Rue De Louvain: work in three phases, from May to November 2026, from May to October 2027, then from May to August 2028.
Park maintenance: contracts from May 1, 2026 to October 31, 2028; 26 hectares will be added to the park in 2027 in the Boisé Ouest sector.
Rental of the screener and loader tractor from June 20 to October 15, 2026.

grand-parc-ouest.description: The largest municipal park in Canada, being assembled: land acquisitions, Anse-à-l'Orme, Cap-Saint-Jacques, Bois-de-la-Roche, parc-nature des Sources.

etapes.titre: More money for the stone walls
etapes.texte: The City is adding $162,897.98 to the contract with Les Constructions H2D inc. to rebuild heritage walls along chemin de Senneville, bringing the contract to $1,174,331.77. According to the file, buried stones, surplus mortar and a deteriorated culvert explain the increase; the work, 60% complete as of December 1, 2025, resumes on May 15, 2026.

The City is filing an application for the Cap-Saint-Jacques sector, described as covering 330 hectares, for the international Urban Night Sky Place designation from DarkSky International. The filing involves no spending; the City commits to producing a lighting management plan, bringing its light fixtures up to standard, and keeping the site accessible in the evening.

etapes.titre: Two sectors listed as natural environments
etapes.texte: The City is listing the parc-nature des Sources (38.32 ha) and the Anse-à-l'Orme sector of the Grand parc de l'Ouest (429 ha) in the Répertoire des milieux naturels protégés et contributifs à la biodiversité de l'agglomération, along with conservation plans. It is also taking note of the 2025 area summary.

The City is awarding Gendron Gestion Civil inc. the contract to rebuild the culvert under chemin Senneville, as part of the modernization of the Bois-de-la-Roche agricultural hub, for a total expense of $481,850.45. The work includes the new culvert, roadway resurfacing, and replacement of the guardrails.

aSurveiller.texte: Expected completion of the stone wall work on chemin de Senneville: July 10, 2026.
Filing of the Cap-Saint-Jacques lighting management plan: February 2027.
Response from DarkSky International on the designation: April 2027.

itinerance.description: Support for organizations, warming centres and shelters for people experiencing homelessness.
itinerance.enBref: The City lends municipal buildings to organizations to set up warming centres and funds organizations that work with people experiencing homelessness. It is also renewing a Ville-Marie public works team that handles homelessness-related cleanliness in several boroughs. Lastly, it is setting up a framework to receive private donations for housing and shelter.

etapes.texte: The City is lending three buildings free of charge until April 30, 2026: the church at 5600, 12e Avenue to the Centre des Femmes de convictions de Montréal, the former Recluses Missionnaires monastery at 12050, boulevard Gouin Est to Projets Autochtones du Québec, and the Bain St-Denis at 7075, rue Saint-Hubert to L'Amour en Action SYL DAN. For the monastery, it is transferring $97,000 from the Service de l'habitation to the Service de la gestion et de la planification des immeubles.

Verdun is paying $12,950 to the Société de développement social to keep two outreach workers from January 5 to February 6, 2026. Ahuntsic-Cartierville is increasing to $126,615.07, taxes included, the contract awarded to Les services de cohabitation sociale COHAB inc. for a warming centre during winter 2025-2026.

The City is granting $5,407,736 to 15 organizations and $3,942,461 more to 10 already-funded organizations, until December 31, 2028, under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs. The projects deal with the inclusion of people experiencing homelessness, cohabitation in public space and awareness-raising.

etapes.titre: Private donations and Bain St-Denis fit-out
etapes.texte: Council is adopting a framework to receive private cash donations for housing, shelter and social cohabitation; donors will not choose which projects are funded. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie is transferring $250,000 from its surplus for the fit-out work on the temporary warming centre at the Bain Saint-Denis, and city council is adopting a declaration of support for people experiencing homelessness.

etapes.titre: Nuit des sans-abri and Notre-Dame encampments
etapes.texte: The City is paying $90,000 to the Réseau d'aide aux personnes seules et itinérantes de Montréal, that is $30,000 per year, for the 2026, 2027 and 2028 editions of the Nuit des sans-abri. It is also granting $149,520, taxes included, to Mission Old Brewery to help people from the rue Notre-Dame encampment area move toward shelter and housing.

aSurveiller.texte: Mission Old Brewery's mandate in the rue Notre-Dame encampment area ends on October 18, 2026.
The agreement between Ville-Marie and Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles for the public works team runs until May 15, 2027.
Financial support under the Programme itinérance et milieux inclusifs ends on December 31, 2028.

logement.description: Grants, land and projects for social, affordable or student housing, including those of the SHDM and the OMHM.
logement.enBref: The City approves the 2026 budgets of the Société d'habitation et de développement de Montréal (SHDM) and the Office municipal d'habitation de Montréal (OMHM). It transfers or acquires land for social housing, pays grants to organizations building housing, and signs funding agreements with the Société d'habitation du Québec. It also amends the by-law requiring developers to include social and affordable housing.

etapes.texte: The City accepts, free of charge, half of the rights to a 3,658.8 square-metre site on rue Jolicoeur, in Pierrefonds-Roxboro, from the Government of Canada. It sells, with no consideration, a 789.6 square-metre site on boulevard de l'Acadie to the Coopérative d'habitation Monde-Uni, which must build 26 housing units there, and authorizes a devaluation of $110,000.

The executive committee approves two 2025-2026 funding agreements with the Société d'habitation du Québec for temporary shelter and housing search assistance. After a public consultation meeting held on February 26, 2026, city council amends the by-law on the supply of social, affordable and family housing: it now applies only to projects over 18,000 square metres and requires 20% of units to be off-market.

The City adds $877,312 to its assistance for Mission Unitaînés for a 100-unit building for seniors in Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve. It grants $581,845 to the Coopérative d'habitation Monde-Uni for the Acadie project.

etapes.titre: Purchase of land in Le Sud-Ouest
etapes.texte: The City purchases, for $9,293,113 plus taxes, a vacant 1,535.1 square-metre site near rue Chatham and rue William, for social housing purposes. It also removes 11 lots in Ville-Marie and Le Sud-Ouest from the list of properties subject to the right of first refusal for social housing.

aSurveiller.texte: Deadline set for the sale of the site on rue Chatham and rue William: August 12, 2026.
For the SHDM's 72-unit project on 2e Avenue: public call for tenders in late summer or early fall 2026, construction start by the end of 2026, and delivery in May 2028.
Occupancy expected by April 30, 2027 at the latest for the 350 affordable units at the Technopôle Angus.

louvain-est.description: The neighbourhood being built on City-owned land in Ahuntsic-Cartierville: acquisitions, soil decontamination, street names, temporary developments.

etapes.texte: City council amended two leases for sites south of rue de Louvain and west of boulevard Saint-Laurent: a 2,787-square-metre site leased to the Société de transport de Montréal for $49,293 total, and an 836-square-metre site leased to a paid parking company for $45,049 before taxes.

The City is extending, free of charge, the loan of a 10,000-square-foot site to an organization that grows a vegetable garden there, and of a 3,316-square-metre site to an urban agriculture organization for sunflowers and a greenhouse. City council also agreed to prepare, on its own, a free lease of 78,244 square feet, at the southeast corner of rue de Louvain Ouest and avenue de l'Esplanade, for programming activities.

etapes.titre: Contract to redevelop rue de Louvain
etapes.texte: The borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension awarded a company the redevelopment of rue de Louvain between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel, for a maximum of $8,199,514.82 including taxes, and authorized total spending of $11,192,464.62. The work covers sewers, water mains, lighting, traffic lights, sidewalks, the bike path and plantings.

etapes.titre: The central street gets a name
etapes.texte: City council named the new street at the heart of the eco-district "avenue des Solidarités." The name comes from a public call for proposals held in fall 2024.

etapes.titre: Programming and events on the site
etapes.texte: The borough granted $35,000 to an organization to design and run the Esplanade-Louvain temporary space, at 150, rue de Louvain Ouest, from June 9 to December 31, 2026. It also authorized, on a vacant lot at 50 and 150, rue de Louvain Ouest, an event-based and temporary use: multimedia activity, shows, street food, a drinking establishment and recreational activities.

etapes.titre: New street, networks and remediated soil
etapes.texte: The City awarded a company a contract worth $10,311,940.25 including taxes to build a street with sewer, water main, roadway, lighting and soil management in the eco-district, for total spending of $15,366,336, and added a net $2,007,312.15 to remediate the soil of the former gas station area. The borough also adopted a second draft resolution authorizing the demolition of a building on avenue de l'Esplanade and rue de Louvain Ouest and the construction of a group of buildings.

aSurveiller.texte: The rue de Louvain worksite between parc Frédéric-Back and boulevard Saint-Michel will take place in three phases: May to November 2026, May to October 2027, then May to August 2028.
The loan of the site for sunflowers and the greenhouse runs from November 1, 2026 to October 31, 2027.
The lease for programming activities covers two periods from April 1 to October 31, in 2026 and in 2027.
Four other public spaces on the site remain to be named by the time the developments are completed, expected around 2032.
The parking lease with the Société de transport de Montréal begins October 1, 2026, for three years and a maximum of 92 days per year.

matieres-residuelles.description: Collections, sorting centres, biomethanation and ecocentres.
matieres-residuelles.enBref: This year, the City is adjusting collection days and frequency in several boroughs, buying bins, and extending food waste treatment contracts while waiting for the Montréal-Est biomethanation centre to come into service. It is also awarding services related to ecocentres and former disposal sites. The 2025 residual materials management report and the accountability report on the 2020-2025 master plan were tabled at the urban agglomeration council.

etapes.texte: The City is extending, first by six months, then by another six months, the contracts of Recyclage Notre-Dame inc. for composting or biomethanation of food waste from the east of the agglomeration, until February 28, 2027. The materials are transferred in Montréal-Est, then composted in Saint-Thomas-de-Joliette and in Moose Creek, Ontario, because the start-up of the Montréal-Est centre is not confirmed.

Several boroughs are awarding hydro-excavation contracts including residual materials treatment, following public call for tenders 25-21256. These services are used to dig with pressurized water near water and sewer pipes, until December 31, 2028.

The City is extending by 12 months the contracts of Waste Connections of Canada inc. / Enviro Connexions for the collection and disposal of garbage from front-load and semi-underground containers, maintained until October 31, 2027. It is also extending until October 31, 2027 the supply and transport of containers for the Saint-Laurent ecocentre, a contract assigned to GFL Environmental inc.

Recyc-Matelas inc. is awarded the contract for the collection, transport and recovery of mattresses and box springs from the agglomeration's ecocentres, for $734,690.25 taxes included over 28 months. The City is also retaining Consultants AECOM inc. and Terrapex Environnement ltée for studies related to construction on former disposal sites, and is extending the discharge authorization management software of Diffusion Solutions Intégrées inc.

aSurveiller.texte: Recyclage Notre-Dame inc.'s food waste treatment contracts run until February 28, 2027; the City may terminate them with 30 days' notice if the Montréal-Est centre becomes fully operational.

Collection schedules change on November 1, 2026 in Ahuntsic-Cartierville and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, where the spacing out of garbage collection is done in two phases, in fall 2026 and fall 2027.
The loan of dishware, water fountains and sorting stations is offered until the contribution is used up, and by December 31, 2026 at the latest.
Garbage collection by containers and the supply of containers at the Saint-Laurent ecocentre are provided until October 31, 2027.
The discharge authorization management software is extended from October 12, 2026 to October 11, 2029.

namur-hippodrome.description: The new neighbourhood on the site of the former Blue Bonnets racetrack: sale of land, loan by-laws, waterworks for the Namur–De la Savane sector.
namur-hippodrome.enBref: This year, the City is preparing the ground, both literally and financially, for the future neighbourhood on the site of the former racetrack. It obtained more time from the Québec government to sell a first piece of land, guaranteed a loan for studies, and adopted two loan by-laws for streets, sewers and waterworks in the sector. At the same time, it is leasing parcels of the site to organizations for temporary uses.

etapes.titre: More time to sell a first piece of land
etapes.texte: The Québec government grants the City a delay until October 31, 2027 to sell a first piece of land on the site, located west of boulevard Décarie and south of rue Paré. According to the file, the postponement does not entail any financial compensation, and the other conditions of the 2017 transfer deed remain the same.

City council approves a City guarantee of $2,000,000 in favour of the Canada Infrastructure Bank, for a loan to the GALOPH organization that will be used to pay for feasibility studies for the residential project. On the same day, council rejects a motion from the Official Opposition on governance and asset management in the development of the neighbourhood.

The City adopts a $29,000,000 loan to develop the neighbourhood's public domain: soil remediation, sewers and waterworks, street redevelopment, fees and land purchases. It also adopts a $12,000,000 loan to build main water mains between boulevard Cavendish, in Saint-Laurent, and rue Isabella, in Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce.

etapes.titre: Project for four buildings on rue Namur
etapes.texte: The borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce adopts a draft resolution authorizing the construction of four buildings, in four phases, at 7301 boulevard Décarie and 5150-5160 rue Namur, one of which is to house a municipal sports and recreation centre. The developer will pay $3,200,000 for public facilities and equipment in the sector, and a public consultation meeting will be held.

aSurveiller.texte: The sale of a first piece of land must be completed no later than October 31, 2027.
The federal grant is conditional on the infrastructure being completed by 2031.
The temporary leases end on April 30, 2027 (MultiCaf), March 31, 2028 (Polliflora) and April 30, 2028 (transition nursery).

parcs.description: Development and renovation of parks, including the Grand parc de l'Ouest.
parcs.enBref: The City is funding the design and redevelopment work of parks in several boroughs, from the selection of design teams to construction contracts. It is also active in the Grand parc de l'Ouest: repairs to heritage walls, rebuilding a culvert, listing natural environments in the Répertoire de l'agglomération, and filing an application for an "Urban Night Sky Place" designation. Several projects are paid for by Montréal's participatory budget or by the environmental liability reserve.

etapes.texte: City council awards a professional services contract to the winning team of the architecture competition for the bibliothèque Caroline-Dawson and the redevelopment of the parc Le Prévost, for a total expense of $10,559,257.81, taxes included [CM26 0082]. It also pays $174,471.56 net to Verdun, from the environmental liability reserve, for environmental and geotechnical studies before rebuilding the play structures at the parc Monseigneur-J.-A.-Richard [CM26 0093].

The boroughs award work contracts: parc Mackenzie-King [CA26 170129], parc canin Alexis-Nihon [CA26 08 235], parc Monseigneur-Langlois [CA26 210113], parc Percy-Walters [CA26 240242], parc J.O.R.-Leduc [CA26 20 0291] and parc Baldwin, for a total expense of $4,222,952.86, taxes included [CA26 25 210]. Several of these projects come from the 2nd edition of Montréal's participatory budget.

aSurveiller.texte: Work on parc Percy-Walters from July to November 2026, with a follow-up in spring 2027.
Work on parc Denise-Morelle from early August 2026 to November 2026.
Selection of the winner of the public art competition for parc des Eaux-Cachées in October 2026, contract in December 2026, installation of the artwork in 2028.
For the Cap-Saint-Jacques application: lighting plan filed in February 2027, response from DarkSky expected in April 2027, site compliance in April 2032.
Final acceptance of the parc du Bassin-à-Bois work expected in June 2027.

pietonnisation.description: Pedestrian streets, public squares and commercial animation ordinances.
pietonnisation.enBref: This year, the City and the boroughs are organizing the 2026 season of pedestrian streets and public squares. They adopt funding rules, pay out money to commercial development corporations, then issue the ordinances that close streets to cars and regulate sales, noise and occupation of the roadway. At the end of the season, reopening schedules are adjusted and two files concern the status and name of public squares.

etapes.titre: Settlement of a dispute over a public square
etapes.texte: The Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie borough settles out of court, for $41,686.46, a lawsuit related to the development work on the public square at the corner of rue Beaubien Est and rue Boyer. The settlement is concluded without admission of liability.

etapes.titre: Rules and money for the 2026 season
etapes.texte: Ville-Marie adopts a by-law setting the conditions for grants to its commercial development corporations to pedestrianize streets, with applications to be submitted by February 16, 2026 at the latest. The executive committee then authorizes transfers of $2,694,500 to six boroughs for pedestrian streets on commercial arteries.

The boroughs pay out amounts to commercial development corporations and their projects: $102,045 for rue Villeray, $375,500 for rue Sainte-Catherine Est and $67,500 for avenue Lacombe. Outremont allocates $105,000, net of taxes, to the pedestrianization of avenue Bernard.

Le Plateau-Mont-Royal awards a contract for $287,724.94, taxes included, to provide on-demand transportation for people with reduced mobility and seniors on avenue du Mont-Royal, and bans amplified instruments on its pedestrian streets. Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve temporarily removes 113 paid parking spaces, Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce authorizes a commercial promotion on a closed street on avenue de Monkland, and the City pays $40,000 to animate the Notre-Dame Ouest pedestrian street.

etapes.titre: Status, name and end of season
etapes.texte: City council changes the status of a 899-square-metre lot, at the corner of rue Sherbrooke Est and boulevard Langelier, from a street (public square) to a local park, and names the public square at the corner of rue Charleroi and avenue L'Archevêque « place Chez-Marguerite ». Le Plateau-Mont-Royal divides avenue du Mont-Royal into three sections with separate reopening dates.

aSurveiller.texte: Reopening of avenue du Mont-Royal: between Saint-Denis and Resther on September 30, 2026, between Saint-Laurent and Saint-Denis on October 15, 2026.
Full reopening of avenue Bernard to traffic starting September 25, 2026.
The pedestrian streets and public squares of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce (avenue Royal, avenue Madison, Placette CDN) remain closed to cars until October 31, 2026.
Boroughs' accounting in November 2026 and return of unspent amounts in December 2026.
The on-demand transportation contract on avenue du Mont-Royal covers the period up to December 31, 2027; the contribution for avenue Lacombe runs until December 31, 2028.

plan-urbanisme.description: The PUM and the concordance by-laws each borough adopts to comply with it.

etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville amends its urban planning by-law for the planting, maintenance, protection and felling of trees. Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie revises its urban planning, special projects and demolition by-laws, and Saint-Léonard does the same for its special projects and demolitions, after public consultations held on February 26 and February 11, 2026.

The borough extends its list of heritage-interest buildings, regulates lodging and service establishments for people in residential instability, and amends its by-laws on demolition, special projects and site planning and architectural integration plans. A public assembly was held on March 18, 2026, and a written consultation from March 11 to 18, 2026.

The borough changes the heights, uses and site coverage ratio in the sector bounded by avenue Papineau, avenue Émile-Journault, avenue André-Grasset and rue Legendre Est. It also increases the permitted heights on sections of rue Lajeunesse, between boulevard Crémazie and boulevard Henri-Bourassa.

etapes.titre: Requests for extension to the ministry
etapes.texte: Ahuntsic-Cartierville requests twelve more months, until June 16, 2027, to adopt its concordance by-laws. L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève requests six more months, citing staff shortages, the complexity of its territory and the fall 2025 election.

Ville-Marie amends its urban planning by-law and its by-laws on special projects, demolition, authorization certificates and cadastral operations. After the public consultation of March 25, 2026, the City revised the view corridor and height plans; the by-law allows a maximum height of 103 m on the block of the former terrasse Peel and makes certain work in the declared heritage site of Mont-Royal subject to approval.

Saint-Léonard takes note of two correction minutes signed on March 19, 2026, which correct the name of a school and the identification of a building on boulevard Provencher. Ahuntsic-Cartierville then adopts its by-law on the demolition of buildings, after a public consultation assembly held on June 23, 2026.

aSurveiller.texte: L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève indicates it wants to present its project to elected officials starting mid-June 2026 and hold a public consultation in September or October 2026.

The Minister of Municipal Affairs has set June 16, 2027, as the deadline for Saint-Léonard to adopt all its concordance by-laws; other blocks are announced, including the replacement of the zoning by-law.
Ahuntsic-Cartierville requests an extension until June 16, 2027, to adopt its concordance by-laws.
Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension has until June 17, 2027, to update its by-laws; its zoning by-law must be replaced in 2027.

securite-publique.description: The Service de police de la Ville de Montréal: contracts, neighbourhood police stations, city council motions.
securite-publique.enBref: This year, the City is funding and equipping its police service: a loan for specialized equipment, purchases of vehicles and ammunition, maintenance and service contracts for SPVM buildings. It is also renewing leases for neighbourhood police stations and premises, lending police officers to the RCMP and the Sûreté du Québec, and accepting grants. Borough councils have adopted motions of support for the SPVM following a shooting that occurred on June 22, 2026.

etapes.texte: The urban agglomeration council adopts a by-law authorizing a loan of $10,880,000 to buy and replace specialized public safety equipment between 2026 and 2030. The by-law must be approved by the Minister of Municipal Affairs.

The City buys motorcycles, two pickup trucks for the mounted unit, and a patrol boat with its trailer. It also enters into an agreement to supply 9 mm practice ammunition used for police firearms training and requalification.

The City extends housekeeping services at headquarters, maintenance of the computer-aided dispatch system software, and the SPVM's mail service. It also awards contracts for meals for detained persons and for carpentry and painting services in the service's buildings.

aSurveiller.texte: The lease for the metro unit premises of neighbourhood police station 50, at 888 boulevard De Maisonneuve Est, begins on February 1, 2027.
The patrol boat and its trailer must be delivered no later than March 1, 2027.
The extension of the computer-aided dispatch software maintenance contract runs until May 4, 2027.
Work to replace the oil heating system at the mounted unit building must be completed by September 30, 2027.
Neighbourhood police station 46's "Fèves au lard" day takes place on October 23, 2026.

velo.titre: Cycling: REV, bike paths and BIXI
velo.description: The Réseau express vélo, bike paths and lanes, and the self-service bike system.
velo.enBref: This year, the City is buying bikes, docking points and station parts for the BIXI system, and having new stations installed as part of street worksites. It is also funding the repair of existing bike paths, including the REV Lajeunesse, and formalizing the rent for Hydro-Québec land crossed by bike paths. Boroughs, for their part, oversee the development and maintenance of their own bike paths.

etapes.texte: Outremont authorizes spending of $100,000, taxes included, for concrete, de-icing salt and abrasives intended in particular for bike paths. Ahuntsic-Cartierville awards Déneigement et Excavation M. Gauthier inc. the rental of a mini sweeper with operator for spring cleaning of paths under 1.8 metres wide, for $153,395.05, taxes included.

etapes.titre: Sustainable mobility corridors in the east
etapes.texte: City council adds $3,400,000, taxes included, to the contract with Bruneau Électrique inc. for traffic lights, civil and electrical work and bike paths in Ville-Marie and Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, on rue Hochelaga and rue du Havre. The contract reaches $11,399,999.99, taxes included.

City council approves a $125,167.62 agreement, taxes included, with Hydro-Québec for rent from 2014 to 2025 on 19 plots of land used for bike paths, parks and community gardens. It then approves a 10-year lease, for a total rent of $46,896, taxes included, to lease about 366 square metres in Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles for use as a bike path.

etapes.titre: Repair of the REV Lajeunesse and rue Lajoie
etapes.texte: Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension offers to take charge of repairing sections of the REV Lajeunesse, between rue Jarry and boulevard Crémazie, and city council accepts this offer as well as Ville-Marie's offer for roadway and bike path work under the Plan Vélo 2019. Outremont tables a draft by-law to convert the shared lane on avenue Lajoie, between Stuart and Outremont, into a one-way bike path.

aSurveiller.texte: For the REV Lajeunesse, the file indicates a call for tenders in May 2026, contract awards in June, and work from July to August 2026.
The UCI Road World Championships are held in Montréal from September 20 to 27, 2026; sections along the route are targeted by roadway work in Ville-Marie.
The repair of the bike path on rue De Louvain, between the west side of rue d'Iberville and boulevard Saint-Michel, is budgeted at $570,000 in 2027.
Work on the sustainable mobility corridors resumes in spring 2026, for completion in spring or summer 2026.
